scenario: Peter puts on some music in the office and it starts a friendly debate — love it or hate it. The whole episode contrasts verb + -ing and verb + to-infinitive with likes and dislikes. Pol says, 'I love listening to music while I work.' Den disagrees: 'I hate hearing music. I need to concentrate.' Alex jokes, 'I enjoy sleeping, and music helps me to relax.' Valery says, 'I prefer to work in silence. I stopped listening to music years ago.' Kate tries to keep everyone happy: 'Let's try to find a fair rule.' A neat meaning-change pair slips in: 'Den stopped drinking coffee' (gave it up) vs 'Pol stopped to drink his smoothie' (paused in order to). In the end they agree on headphones. Warm, light disagreement, nobody is angry. Use clear patterns: like/love/hate/enjoy/prefer + -ing; want/need/decide/try + to-infinitive. Short B1 sentences.
